body: this could be created with `new SearchResults` as well, but I see the point in the explicitly created object too
not sure if we need that test, but we could assert that scheduleRender isn't called when initialResults isn't provided

this line seems to imply that _initialSearchResults isn't `Record<string, SearchResults>`, but rather `Record<string, Pick<SearchResults, "_state" | "_rawResults">>` (and even then state is actually PlainSearchParameters, so it's more: `Record<string, Pick<SearchResults, "_rawResults"> & { _state: PlainSearchParameters }>`).

I think it makes sense to accept the bare minimum as it's easier to reconstruct the class in index than looping before passing it to _initialResults, but the type should be consistent IMO

as an alternative, would it make sense to emit a "result" event from the relevant helper? It should do almost the same, but the flow is a little closer, as it can use the already existing event handler
I think there's value in seeing all the object fields in the test. Both ways are fine to me.
Tests fail without `if (indexInitialResults)` so to me it's already covered in some ways.
You're right, this is easier to deal with user-land. Addressed in ebe44957f9d075fbe2b8c354d16452fbf74f34ad.
I pushed another simplification in d291709666d69c3c68b021a57df5162094cf121f.
I assume this is to test adding widgets in the same tick after the instance is started. Is it worth also testing adding widgets before, then starting?
Why do you think it's more error-prone? Since we'd be using the helper API, we don't have to be concerned with reproducing what it does under the hood.

The code path for this scenario is covered here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4967/files#diff-d2c89d817ae8132531fe3e185d64d50ce86e18d4306c93d979c39dd2a4e1fda0R863-R879.

Adding widgets prior to starting the search has never scheduled a search so I don't think it's required that we add another test for this here.

We never emit the "result" event in InstantSearch, the Helper does internally. So that would be a new concept in the codebase – a new API we need to grasp. And we need to give it the correct `results` and the correct `state` (the distinction of helper and derived helper is already confusing in `index`).

On the other hand, we created `scheduleRender` in InstantSearch and already use it in `InstantSearch` and `index`.
